correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real L4 unit vectors, Hölder bounds all mixed quartic integrals and norm outputs lie in compact interval [3/4,5/4] for tau<=1/4. Uniform first-order Taylor of both fourth roots and of the t-power mean for fixed 1<=t<4 yields F_t=1+(tau/2)D+O_t(tau^2), D=∫xy(x²-y²). Symbolically and independently checked exact integrand square: ||xy+(x²-y²)/sqrt2||_2²=1+sqrt2 D on unit pairs. So slope >=-1/(2sqrt2), sharp on x=af+bg,y=-bf+ag for disjoint unit f,g with a⁴=(2+sqrt3)/4,b⁴=(2-sqrt3)/4. The quadratic Q=0 forces only two pointwise x/y ratios; splitting their measurable sets and the two fourth-power normalization equations forces f,g both unit, exhausting all fixed extremizers. Uniform remainder and infimum comparison imply asymptotic near-minimizer iff ||Q||_2->0, and excess epsilon tau implies the quantified Q² bound. Independent symbolic identity confirms algebra; random finite checks alone would not suffice for all L4 spaces.
residual_risks: Does not classify minimizers at fixed positive tau; fixed exponent t<4, real scalars and only Q-defect quantitative stability rather than L4 distance stability.
